intro: The top of the loop. Ten minutes. This file decides who is allowed to decide what — including which decisions an agent gets to make alone.

ask.q: The objective this quarter — a number and a date.
ask.example: $4.2M revenue by Dec 31 at or under $58 blended CAC

ask.q: How many agents, and what are they?
What will you not do to hit the number?
ask.help: The question that makes this file worth writing. If there's no answer, the number owns you.

ask.q: For each node, name the accountable human and the agent.
ask.help: "Agent-first" still means a named human reads the output. A node with no name on it is the first place this breaks.

ask.q: What can an agent decide on its own, reviewed after the fact?
What must an agent propose and a human approve before it ships?
ask.help: Anything with the brand name on it, any spend change, any offer — at minimum.

ask.q: What does a human decide outright, with the agent only supporting?
What must make an agent stop and escalate?
ask.help: Write triggers, not principles. "Spend variance over 15%" escalates; "use good judgment" does not.

ask.q: Who writes the "what it means" paragraph on the weekly rollup?
ask.help: An agent can draft the numbers. Someone has to say what they mean and sign it.
